covers.quote: When you have links in the materials, you need to:

rules.quote: provide clear link text
rules.specification: Assess whether the intended users can understand the link's purpose or destination from its wording and context. The page does not prescribe particular link labels.
rules.violation_condition: A link has text that does not make its purpose or destination understandable in context.
when: Applies when Easy Read materials contain links.
rules.why: G-1 separates this textual requirement from the publishing section; link clarity and visual link styling are different checks.

covers.quote: When you have links in the materials, you need to:

rules.quote: spell out the URL next to the linked text.
rules.violation_condition: Linked text appears without its URL written out next to it.
when: Applies when Easy Read materials contain links.
rules.why: G-1: the missing written URL is independently flaggable, rather than part of a general publishing rule.

rules.quote: Include examples throughout to help explain ideas and concepts.
rules.specification: The page does not define how frequently examples must appear or which concepts require them. Do not invent a numerical quota.
rules.violation_condition: Ideas and concepts are presented without explanatory examples distributed through the material.
rules.why: G-5 distinguishes the surrounding planning advice from this observable requirement for explanatory content.

rules.quote: Check your content reads between a year 4 to year 6 reading level.
rules.specification: The required range is stated, but no reading-level assessment method is specified. A checker needs an agreed method rather than silently choosing a formula.
rules.violation_condition: The content has a reading level outside the year 4 to year 6 range.
rules.why: This states a property of the resulting text, not merely a proofreading activity under G-5.

rules.quote: Use simple words and grammar
rules.specification: Assess simplicity for the intended users. Necessary difficult words are permitted, subject to the separate bolding and definition requirements; syllable count alone does not determine a violation.
rules.violation_condition: The text uses words or grammatical constructions that are unnecessarily difficult for its intended Easy Read users.
when: Important difficult words may be retained when needed.
rules.why: G-2 preserves the necessary-difficult-word case; simple language and adult-appropriate language produce different findings.

rules.quote: don’t use childish language if the users are adults.
rules.specification: Distinguish language that addresses adults as children from language that is simply easy to understand.
rules.violation_condition: Material intended for adults uses childish language.
when: Applies when the intended users are adults.
rules.why: G-2 records the audience condition; childish tone is a separate failure from linguistic complexity.

covers.quote: A difficult word might have 3 or more syllables.

examples.note: The supplied text extraction does not preserve any bold formatting, so this example cannot establish which words are bold.

parts.quote: Immunisation protects your baby from some diseases. Immunisation means a doctor or nurse gives your baby a needle with a vaccineinside. The vaccine is the medicine that protects your baby from some diseases.

rules.quote: If you need to use a difficult word, write it in bold.
rules.specification: An agreed criterion for difficulty is needed. Three or more syllables is a possible indicator, not a categorical definition of a difficult word.
rules.violation_condition: A necessary difficult word is not in bold.
when: Applies when a difficult word needs to be retained.
rules.why: G-2 keeps the necessary-word condition with the bolding check; bolding and defining a word are separate requirements.

examples.note: This is the manual's example as supplied, including the apparent missing space in ‘vaccineinside’.

parts.quote: Immunisation protects your baby from some diseases. Immunisation means a doctor or nurse gives your baby a needle with a vaccineinside. The vaccine is the medicine that protects your baby from some diseases.

rules.quote: Define the difficult word in the next sentence or phrase.
rules.specification: The placement requirement is explicit, but identifying difficult words requires an agreed audience-sensitive criterion.
rules.violation_condition: A difficult word is not defined in the next sentence or phrase.
when: Applies when a difficult word is used.
rules.why: The missing or misplaced definition is independently flaggable from missing bold formatting.

covers.quote: a word list if there are a lot of difficult words
At the end, add:

rules.quote: If you have defined a lot of words, include a glossary at the end of your document.
rules.specification: The page does not quantify ‘a lot’. An agreed threshold is needed before implementing a count-based check.
rules.violation_condition: A document with many defined or difficult words has no word list at the end.
when: Applies when a lot of words have been defined or a lot of difficult words are used.
rules.why: G-2 and G-4 consolidate the two statements requiring the same end-of-document word list.

rules.quote: Call it a word list.
rules.violation_condition: The glossary is labelled with a name other than ‘word list’.
when: Applies when the document contains a glossary.
rules.why: Naming an existing glossary incorrectly is a different finding from omitting the required word list.

covers.quote: Only use questions in headings for Easy Read.

rules.quote: Avoid questions in the text
rules.violation_condition: A question appears in the body text rather than in a heading.
when: Questions in headings are permitted.
rules.why: G-3 records the heading permission as a limit; G-4 absorbs the body's restatement.

rules.quote: If you need information from people, follow questions with practical examples so people know how to respond.
rules.violation_condition: A question seeking information from the reader is not followed by practical examples showing how to respond.
when: Applies to questions used to obtain information from people.
rules.why: G-2 keeps the information-gathering condition with this check; missing response examples are distinct from a question's location.

covers.quote: This is not always possible for complex information.

rules.quote: Keep your Easy Read brief.
rules.specification: No word or page limit is supplied. A checker must distinguish avoidable length from length needed for complex information.
rules.violation_condition: The Easy Read material is unnecessarily long, beyond what is needed to explain its information.
when: Complex information may make brevity impractical.
rules.why: G-2 retains the complexity exception; G-5 excludes the subsequent advice about considering separate documents.

rules.quote: Only use bold for headings and difficult words.
rules.specification: Heading status is identifiable, but determining whether other bold text consists of difficult words requires an agreed difficulty criterion.
rules.violation_condition: Bold formatting is applied to text that is neither a heading nor a difficult word.
when: Bold is permitted for headings and difficult words.
rules.why: G-2 and G-3 keep both allowed uses within one check for inappropriate bold.

covers.quote: At the beginning of the content:

rules.quote: introduce your organisation
rules.violation_condition: The beginning of the content does not introduce the organisation.
when: The introduction belongs at the beginning of the content.
rules.why: G-1: this required introductory content is a child rule, not part of a catch-all context rule.

covers.quote: At the beginning of the content:

rules.quote: explain how to use it – images with text, difficult words and links
rules.violation_condition: The beginning of the content does not explain how to use its images with text, difficult words and links.
when: The explanation belongs at the beginning of the content.
Explain the listed features that the material uses.
rules.why: G-1 separates the usage explanation from the other independently required introductory content.

covers.quote: At the beginning of the content:

rules.quote: add words to reassure people that it’s okay to ask someone else to help them read it
rules.violation_condition: The beginning of the content lacks reassurance that readers can ask someone else to help them read it.
when: The reassurance belongs at the beginning of the content.
rules.why: G-1: reassurance about reading assistance is an independently checkable content requirement.

covers.quote: At the beginning of the content:

rules.quote: explain how the Easy Read relates to other content – as a summary or guide
rules.violation_condition: The beginning of the content does not explain how the Easy Read relates to the other content it summarises or guides readers through.
when: Applies where the Easy Read relates to other content.
The explanation belongs at the beginning of the content.
rules.why: G-1 separates the explanation of the material's relationship to other content from other context requirements.

covers.quote: At the beginning of the content:

rules.quote: provide a URL or a hyperlink to the standard version (for digital content)
rules.violation_condition: Digital Easy Read content lacks a URL or hyperlink to the standard version at the beginning.
when: Applies to digital content.
The URL or hyperlink belongs at the beginning of the content.
rules.why: G-2 keeps the digital-content condition with the single requirement to link to the standard version.

covers.quote: At the beginning of the content:

rules.quote: include a list of contents if there are several pages.
rules.specification: The page does not quantify ‘several pages’. An agreed page-count threshold is needed.
rules.violation_condition: An Easy Read document with several pages lacks a list of contents at the beginning.
when: Applies when the document has several pages.
The list of contents belongs at the beginning.
rules.why: G-2 retains the length condition; E-4 prevents an invented page threshold being presented as the manual's wording.

covers.quote: At the end, add:

rules.quote: where people can find more information
rules.violation_condition: The end of the content does not tell readers where to find more information.
when: The information belongs at the end of the content.
rules.why: G-1 separates this required closing information from the word-list and contact-information requirements.

covers.quote: At the end, add:

rules.quote: ‘contact us’ information.
rules.violation_condition: The end of the content lacks contact information.
when: The contact information belongs at the end of the content.
rules.why: G-1: missing contact details are independently flaggable; the instruction does not require a literal ‘contact us’ heading.

anchor.quote: If you need to use a difficult word, write it in bold.

covers.quote: A difficult word might have 3 or more syllables.

examples.note: The supplied text extraction does not preserve any bold formatting, so this example cannot establish which words are bold.

parts.quote: Immunisation protects your baby from some diseases. Immunisation means a doctor or nurse gives your baby a needle with a vaccineinside. The vaccine is the medicine that protects your baby from some diseases.

tags.specification: An agreed criterion for difficulty is needed. Three or more syllables is a possible indicator, not a categorical definition of a difficult word.
tags.violation_condition: A necessary difficult word is not in bold.

when: Applies when a difficult word needs to be retained.
rules.why: G-2 keeps the necessary-word condition with the bolding check; bolding and defining a word are separate requirements.

anchor.quote: Define the difficult word in the next sentence or phrase.

parts.quote: Immunisation protects your baby from some diseases. Immunisation means a doctor or nurse gives your baby a needle with a vaccineinside. The vaccine is the medicine that protects your baby from some diseases.

tags.specification: The placement requirement is explicit, but identifying difficult words requires an agreed audience-sensitive criterion.
tags.violation_condition: A difficult word is not defined in the next sentence or phrase.

when: Applies when a difficult word is used.
rules.why: The missing or misplaced definition is independently flaggable from missing bold formatting.
